verdicts.claim: Autocheckpointing is on by default with a threshold of 1000 pages (about 4 MB, overridable at compile time with SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHE
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Autocheckpointing is enabled by default with an interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'; 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off'; wal.html: 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB in size)'

verdicts.claim: All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE. The connection whose COMMIT pushes the WAL past the threshold runs the checkpoint, and the last
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE.'; wal.html: 'run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit' and 'the last connection ... does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers, never invokes the busy-handler... FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE block new writers but not new readers
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: PASSIVE 'busy-handler callback is never invoked'; FULL 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint syncs the WAL before copying into the database and syncs the database before the WAL is reset. With synchronous=NORMAL
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The WAL must be synced ... prior to moving content ... and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL'; 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier'; 'Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL'

verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'three integer columns ... 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked ... second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'; v2: 'upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE ... both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... if the journal or WAL file is larger it is truncated to the limit'
